annotations.text:
A · STRIPPED (same app, less on it)
The default surface is the bar, today’s list and three tabs. Everything else is opt-in in Settings › On screen. First run is one question and a field; what they type decides which page they see first, and that page gets one callout.

B · THREAD (Peggy is a conversation)
Home is a message thread. You type, Peggy answers with what it did, and Sort happens as chips inside her reply. Today is a pinned card that opens the day view. Ideas are long messages she files.

Why: a message field cannot be mistaken for a calendar, and every reply is the explanation you gave Jensen by hand.
Cost: a new shell; a thread is poor at showing a week, so Plan survives as a second screen behind the pinned card.

C · ONE FEED (no tabs)
One scrolling page: Today, Tomorrow, then Needs a day with the Sort rail inline, then Ideas. The bar at the bottom, no navigation at all.

Why: the most literal “as simple as possible”, and every component already exists.
Cost: a busy user gets a long page; Sort and Ideas lose their own room.
